study type: Population-based study (using WHO maternal near-miss criteria)
exposure: Cause of haemorrhage (placental abruption, complications of caesarean section, uterine atony)
outcome: Transfusion requirements (packed red blood cells, Fresh Frozen Plasma)
cohort: Women with major obstetric haemorrhage in the Metro East region, Cape Town, South Africa, from November 2014 to November 2015
finding: Placental abruption and complications of caesarean section were the leading causes of major obstetric haemorrhage, and caesarean section was independently associated with poor maternal outcome.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was independently associated with poor maternal outcome in women experiencing major obstetric hemorrhage.
